chunks: I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was wearing a khazz cloak, its lining was khazz, and a high-quality khazz pallium. So I said: 'Verily, upon me is a garment that I dislike wearing.' He said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'This pallium of mine.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the pallium?' I said: 'It is khazz.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the khazz?' I said: 'Its warp is silk.' He said: 'And what is the matter with the silk?' He said: 'It is not disliked that the warp of the garment be silk, nor its buttons, nor its emblem. But rather, what is disliked is the entirely silk for men; and it is not disliked for women.'

key_terms.إِبْرِيسَم: Ibreesam/Ibrisam — pure raw silk thread; distinct from khazz which blends silk with other fibers.
key_terms.الْمُصْمَت: Al-musmat — a garment made entirely of one material, in this context referring to pure silk with no blending of other fibers.
key_terms.خَزّ: Khazz — a fabric historically woven from silk and wool, widely used in early Islamic society. The permissibility of wearing khazz was a matter of jurisprudential debate.
key_terms.سَدَى: Sada — the warp threads in textile weaving; the longitudinal threads over and under which the weft threads are woven.
key_terms.طَيْلَسَان: Tayalsan — a type of shawl or cloak draped over the shoulders, used by scholars and men of distinction in classical Islamic societies.
key_terms.مَكْرُوه: Makruh — jurisprudentially 'disliked' or 'disapproved'; a category of acts that are not forbidden (haram) but are considered undesirable in Islamic law.

ai.seo_question: Is it allowed for Muslim men to wear khazz fabric with silk threads in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith records a conversation between Abu Dawud Yusuf ibn Ibrahim and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about wearing garments made of khazz — a fabric woven from silk and wool or other fibers. The narrator wore such garments and expressed discomfort, prompting the Imam to clarify the jurisprudential ruling: only garments made entirely (al-musmat) of pure silk are disliked (makruh) for men, while having silk merely in the warp threads, buttons, or decorative emblems does not render the garment makruh. Women are exempt from this ruling entirely.
